newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bundestag passes 1999 tax bill.
newsitem.headline: German Bundestag passes 1999 tax bill.

text.p: Germany's Bundestag lower house of parliament on Thursday passed the final reading of Finance Minister Theo Waigel's 1999 tax reform bill with a majority of 326 to 301 votes.
Counting was continuing in the vote on Waigel's 1998 tax bill, but a similar result was likely.
The two-year package foresees sweeping cuts in income and corporate taxes, to be partly offset by scrapping a range of tax breaks. Overall net tax cuts are targeted at around 30 billion marks.

Passage of the package of tax cuts will now send the bills to the Bundesrat upper house, whose opposition Social Democrat (SPD) majority is expected to vote down the measures on July 4, sending them into parliament's mediation process.
